The exact transmission for a rectangular barrier is T = 1/[1 + V0² sinh²(κa) / (4E(V0−E))].

With E = 0.5 eV and V0 = 2 eV, V0²/(4E(V0−E)) = 4/3, so T = 1/[1 + (4/3) sinh²x], where x = κa.

The approximation is T_approx = 16(0.25)(0.75) e^(−2x) = 3e^(−2x).

The ratio simplifies, using 4e^(−2x) sinh²x = 1 − 2e^(−2x) + e^(−4x):

T_approx/T = 3e^(−2x) + 4e^(−2x) sinh²x = 1 + y + y², where y = e^(−2x).

This ratio is always above 1 and decreases monotonically as x grows. So the condition holds for every larger width exactly when it holds at the threshold width.

Set y + y² = 0.10. Then y = (−1 + √1.4)/2 = 0.091608.

Then 2x = ln(1/0.091608) = ln(10.9162) = 2.39025, so x = 1.19512.

The decay constant is κ = √(1.5/0.0380998) nm⁻¹ = √39.3697 nm⁻¹ = 6.2745 nm⁻¹.

The smallest width is a = x/κ = 1.19512/6.2745 ≈ 0.1905 nm.
